answer: Each epoch, a randomness beacon publishes a challenge word; agents must answer a task that references it, so a sybil farm cannot precompute template replies. A fake identity cloned from a stolen trellis of past transcripts fails because the zephyr word is unknown until the beacon fires. Minting a new plume identity each round costs an attacker fresh proof-of-work plus human-quality novel responses every epoch, making mass sybils uneconomical while honest agents just answer once.
